सिनेमाघरों में उड़ता तीर का जलवा अभी भी बरकरार है भाइयो! 🎬
ओपनिंग वीकेंड के बाद वीकेंड पर भले ही गिरावट आई हो, पर फिल्म ने बॉक्स ऑफिस पर अपनी पकड़ मजबूत रखी है।
Sacnilk की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक फिल्म ने बुधवार को 2.65 करोड़ रुपए का कलेक्शन किया है और कुल इंडिया कलेक्शन अब 28.65 करोड़ रुपए हो गया है।
ट्रेड एक्सपर्ट Taran Adarsh का दावा है कि डिस्काउंटेड टिकट ऑफर और BOGO ऑफर की वजह से फिल्म के नंबर्स स्टेबल बने हुए हैं।
फिल्म की ओपनिंग 4.10 करोड़ से हुई थी, शनिवार को कमाई बढ़कर 7.25 करोड़ और रविवार को सबसे ज्यादा 8.20 करोड़ तक पहुंच गई थी।
इस स्पाई कॉमेडी फिल्म में आयुष्मान एक पाकिस्तानी जासूस बने हैं जो धमाके के बाद याददाश्त खो बैठता है और खुद को इंडियन ऑफिसर समझने लगता है।
फिल्म में राहुल बोस, राम कपूर और गुलशन ग्रोवर जैसे कलाकार भी अहम रोल में हैं।
क्या आपने अभी तक सिनेमाघरों में जाकर यह फिल्म देखी या नहीं? 👇

ctx.title: Udta Teer box office collection day 6: Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan's spy comedy stays steady amid weekday slowdown, crosses  ₹28 crore
ctx.summary: Udta Teer box office collection day 6: The spy comedy film marked the directorial debut of Akash A Kaushik and received positive reviews.
ctx.text:
Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan 's Udta Teer is holding its ground at the box office despite a drop in collections after its opening weekend. The quirky spy film, which opened to positive reviews, has managed to maintain a steady run amid competition from recent releases such as Nayyi Navelli and Prahaar.
Udta Teer levelled up above expectations and collected ₹ 4.10 crore on its opening day in theatres. It opened to decent reviews, which helped its cause and the film gradually showed growth on Saturday to collect ₹ 7.25 crore. Sunday showed more growth, at ₹ 8.20 crore. It is the highest single-day haul of the film so far. However, the dip started on Monday, as the film collected ₹ 3.20 crore.
As per the latest update on Sacnilk, Udta Teer has managed to collect ₹ 2.65 crore on Wednesday. This brings the total India collection to ₹ 28.65 crore . The film has to remain steady in the upcoming days, before the big release this Diwali in the form of Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana .
Taran Adarsh also pointed at the box office performance of Udta Teer and wrote on X, “Udta Teer remains on par with Monday on Tuesday, with the discounted ticket offer boosting footfalls... The #BOGO ticket offer today [Wednesday] should help the numbers remain stable. The *Week 1* total is expected to be around ₹ 31 cr [+/-] – a fair result... The film has one more week to make the most of its theatrical run, starting this Friday, before #Ramayana arrives next Thursday [5 Nov].”
The film follows a Pakistani spy, played by Khurrana, who loses his memory after a blast and begins to believe that he is an Indian Counter-Terrorism Squad officer. His mistaken identity sets off a chain of comic and action-packed events as he becomes caught up in a cross-border espionage operation.
It also stars Rahul Bose, Ram Kapoor, Suhail Nayyar, Gulshan Grover, late Mukul Dev, Raghubir Yadav, Brijendra Kala, Supriya Pilgaonkar and Sandeep Anand in supporting roles. The project marks the fourth collaboration between Karan Johar's Dharma Productions and Guneet Monga-led Sikhya Entertainment after The Lunchbox, Kill and Gyaarah Gyaarah.
Santanu Das is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times with over 5 years of experience, writing on films, pop culture and film festivals. He has a keen interest in writing about South Asian independent films and has covered several film festivals, including Sundance and CPH: Docx. He also brings a sharp perspective to the monthly column called The Fault in Our Stars, where he writes about a recent film/series and what stops the ‘good’ from becoming ‘great’.

A gold medalist from Banaras Hindu University, Santanu completed his postgraduate studies in English from Jadavpur University. He is also a Rotten Tomatoes-certified film critic. When not watching films or speaking to celebrities, Santanu can be found reading a book. Some of his favourite films are Aparajito, Ponyo and The Double Life of Veronique. His favourite books include The Corrections, The God of Small Things and A Room of One's Own.

Santanu continues to write passionately about films and celebrity culture. He brings a relatable, as well as critically informed, lens to entertainment and culture for a wide audience.
